I've been farming for 30 years, since I was 18. My farm is a bit more than 10 mu — 10 mu and a small piece. There are just two of us at home. My husband works construction in the county town, so most days I'm the only one in the fields. I have to watch every yuan because we live on my husband's wages plus what the land gives us.

I split the land into two parts. About 6 mu I keep for wheat and corn, the double crop. The other 4 mu and a bit I plant cotton. Cotton is back-breaking work — you have to pick every boll by hand — but last year the price was decent, and I need the cash income.

For wheat, I always plant around October 10th. I saved some seed from last year but I also bought new improved seed to be safe, about 7 kg per mu. Before planting, I spread base fertilizer — half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Then in March or April, when the wheat is turning green, if it looks yellow I topdress with urea. Last year I used about 13 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, and I got around 400 kg per mu. I'll do the same this year. Fertilizer is dear now, over 100 yuan a bag, but my neighbor Lao Wang cut back last year and his wheat was thin as a comb. I'd rather waste a little money than lose a whole crop. I irrigate 3 times: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The pump electricity costs about 30-40 yuan each time, but without water there's no yield.

For corn, I plant it right after wheat harvest in early June. There's barely a week between harvest and planting — sometimes I don't even plow deep, I just get the machine in and plant. I buy hybrid seed, about 2.5 kg per mu, costs more than wheat seed. I put compound fertilizer down at planting, and if the corn looks pale at the big trumpet stage I add a bit of urea. Corn needs less than wheat, maybe 12 kg nitrogen per mu. I irrigate once or twice depending on the rain. Last year I got about 450 kg per mu.

Cotton is the most work and the most expense. I plant in late April. The insects love cotton — I have to spray 4 or 5 times over the summer, otherwise the worms destroy everything. That costs me 200-300 yuan just for chemicals. I use about 10 kg nitrogen per mu, once at planting and once at flowering. I irrigate twice. The worst is picking in September and October — I have to hire women from the village, paying them by the day. Last year I got about 280 kg per mu of seed cotton. I hope for the same this year, God willing.

My husband comes back for the wheat harvest and corn planting — that's the craziest week. The rest of the season it's mostly me. I try to keep total spending around 3,000 to 3,500 yuan for all inputs. That's most of what we have put aside, but if the weather holds, we should get it back and maybe a little more.
